title: King and pawn against king: the king leads
outcomes: Wins king and pawn against king by bringing the king in front of the pawn first and pushing the pawn only when a push is needed
Holds the draw as the defender by standing in front of the pawn and taking the opposition
Recognises when the plan fails: the defender facing the king with the move against it, a rook pawn with the defender near the corner

steps.text: **King and pawn against king** is decided by the kings more than by the pawn. Attacker: bring your king in front of the pawn and push only when a push is needed (a **rule of thumb**, not a law). Defender: stand in front of the pawn and keep the opposition. Pushing early is the classic way to throw a win away. Watch one win, then test the rule.

steps.caption: White to move. Each of the king moves Kf5, Kd4 and Kf4 wins; the push f4 only draws.

line.say: The king goes first. Kd4 and Kf4 also win here; the push f4 only draws.
White's king keeps going, further ahead of the pawn.
Only now does the pawn move, one square, with the king well ahead of it.
Black's king steps along the back rank.
The pawn steps forward again, protected by the king on g7.
Black's king cannot reach the pawn.
One step from queening, and the king guards the queening square.

claims.statement: White wins from the start position.

steps.text: The plan is a **rule of thumb**; it fails in two ways. The enemy king may cover the squares ahead, so a pawn push is the only winning move. Or nothing wins: the defender faces your king and you are to move, or the pawn is on the edge file with his king near the corner. Ask: can my king get ahead of the pawn, and who is to move?

steps.title: Same pawn, the enemy king one step away
steps.prompt: In the first position the king step wins. Black's king moves one square. Find the winning move again.

steps.title: Same plan, the edge file
steps.prompt: In the first position Black is lost. In the second Black's king is one step nearer the corner. Predict the result.
Before each answer: did you look at the two kings first, or at the pawn? Which of your moves or predictions came from pushing the pawn too early?
